sections.title: Networks and internet operation
sections.text:
**a computer network.**

A network connects devices so they can exchange data and share resources. Connections may use copper cables, fiber-optic links or radio waves. Devices need agreed communication rules, called **protocols**.

**Internet versus World Wide Web.**

The **internet** is a global system of interconnected networks using internet protocols. The **World Wide Web** is a service using linked resources and technologies such as HTTP, browsers and web servers. The web is only one application of the internet. Email, online games, messaging and many other services also use internet connectivity.

**Switch versus router.**

**Switch:** Usually forwards frames among devices on a local network, commonly using link-layer addresses.

**Router:** Forwards packets between IP networks based on routing information.

A home Wi-Fi router often integrates routing, switching, wireless access and other functions in one physical unit.

**TCP versus UDP.**

| TCP | UDP |
|---|---|
| Connection-oriented transport | Connectionless datagram transport |
| Provides reliable ordered byte stream under normal operation | Does not itself guarantee delivery or ordering |
| Handles retransmission and congestion control | Lower protocol overhead in its basic form |
| Common for many traditional web and application connections | Used in DNS, streaming and other applications |
| Not automatically lower latency | Useful when applications implement suitable behavior |

**Important qualification:** HTTP/3 uses QUIC, which operates over UDP while implementing reliability and security features above it. Thus, saying that all HTTP must use TCP is no longer correct.

**DNS.**

DNS stands for **Domain Name System**. It associates human-readable domain names with records, including addresses used to reach servers. For example, a browser can use DNS to obtain a relevant IP address associated with a website name. DNS is a distributed naming system, not one universal computer containing every website's address.

**HTTPS.**

HTTPS is HTTP with a secure transport arrangement, commonly provided through TLS. TLS helps protect confidentiality and integrity of data between the communicating endpoints and authenticates the server under appropriate certificate validation.

**HTTPS does not prove that the website's content is truthful or that the operator is trustworthy.**

A fraudulent website can also use HTTPS.

IP addresses identify network interfaces within an addressing system; IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses and IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses. A local network connects nearby devices, while wide-area networks connect across larger distances. A network interface's link address and an IP address serve different protocol roles. NAT commonly allows several privately addressed devices to share public address resources, but it is not a complete substitute for security controls.

The internet protocol stack separates application behaviour, transport, internet-layer addressing and link delivery. Encapsulation adds the information needed at successive layers. Routing chooses paths between networks, while switching commonly forwards local frames. No single organization stores all internet content or directly manages every link.

To load a secure webpage, a browser determines the destination, obtains relevant DNS records, establishes a suitable secure transport connection, sends an HTTP request and processes the response. It may fetch further resources before rendering the page. DNS caching can reduce repeated lookup work, but records expire and addresses can change. HTTPS protects transport under its trust assumptions, not the truthfulness of a page. [MDN: HTTP overview](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Overview).

sections.title: Signals, modulation and communication quality
sections.text:
**telecommunication.**

Telecommunication is the transmission and reception of information over a distance using suitable physical signals. Examples include a telephone call, radio broadcast, television transmission, satellite internet service and fiber-optic data transfer. The essential elements are:

**Source → Transmitter → Communication channel → Receiver → Destination**

A communication system may also include encoding, modulation, amplification, error correction and other operations.

**Analog versus digital communication.**

An **analog signal** varies continuously over a defined range. A **digital signal** represents information using discrete symbols, commonly binary values.

| Analog communication | Digital communication |
|---|---|
| Information represented continuously | Information represented as discrete symbols |
| Traditional analog radio broadcasting | Modern packet-based digital networks |
| Noise can directly distort the represented signal | Suitable coding can detect/correct certain errors |
| Simple in some applications | Supports compression, encryption and digital processing |

Digital transmission is not immune to interference. If channel conditions become sufficiently poor, errors and complete connection loss can occur.

**modulation.**

Modulation changes some characteristic of a carrier signal to represent information. A high-frequency carrier can support communication through suitable transmitting and receiving equipment. Three familiar carrier characteristics are: Amplitude. Frequency. Phase.

**AM versus FM versus digital QAM.**

| Method | What changes? | Typical application |
|---|---|---|
| AM | Carrier amplitude | AM radio broadcasting |
| FM | Instantaneous carrier frequency | FM radio broadcasting |
| PSK | Carrier phase states | Digital radio links |
| QAM | Amplitude and phase states | Modern broadband digital communication |

**Signal-to-noise ratio.**

The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compares signal power with noise power.

$$\boxed{SNR=\frac{P_{\text{signal}}}{P_{\text{noise}}}}$$

It is often expressed in decibels:

$$SNR_{\mathrm{dB}}=10\log_{10}\left(\frac{P_{\text{signal}}}{P_{\text{noise}}}\right)$$

A higher SNR generally supports more reliable signal recovery, all else being equal. Actual performance also depends on interference, coding, modulation and receiver design.

Digital communication also involves sampling, coding and detection. Error-detection codes can identify certain corrupted patterns; correction requires enough structured redundancy and an appropriate decoder. A simple parity bit detects some errors but does not correct arbitrary ones. Compression reduces representation size, encryption protects confidentiality and error control addresses corruption: these operations have different purposes.

Bandwidth can refer to a frequency range in hertz or, informally, to data capacity in bits per second. Latency is delay. Higher capacity does not remove propagation delay. A hypothetical 80-megabit transfer at a sustained 20 megabits per second takes four seconds before extra delays and overhead. If a file size is supplied in bytes, multiply by eight before dividing by a bit-per-second rate.

sections.title: Cellular mobile communication
sections.text:
**cellular communication.**

Cellular communication is a wireless system in which a service region is divided into smaller coverage areas called **cells**. Base stations serve devices within their coverage regions. The cellular arrangement supports frequency reuse, mobility and efficient sharing of communication resources. A cell is a radio coverage region, not a biological cell.

**frequency reuse.**

Frequency reuse means assigning the same radio-frequency resources in different sufficiently separated areas while controlling interference. This increases the capacity of a cellular network. Modern networks also employ complex interference management, spatial processing and scheduling.

**handover.**

Handover transfers an ongoing mobile connection from one serving cell or radio connection to another as a user moves or network conditions change. For example, a moving vehicle may travel between the coverage regions of neighboring base stations. The network can coordinate this transition.

**Handover is not the same as disconnecting and manually starting a new telephone call.**

**Mobile network generations.**

| Generation | Scientific/technical development |
|---|---|
| 1G | Primarily analog cellular voice |
| 2G | Digital voice and associated messaging/data services |
| 3G | Expanded mobile data and multimedia capabilities |
| 4G | Mobile broadband, commonly IP-based systems |
| 5G | Advanced broadband, low-latency and machine-type communication capabilities |

Radio access connects a device to a base station, while backhaul and the core network carry traffic onward and manage services. Capacity depends on spectrum, signal conditions, scheduling, antennas and user demand. A generation label describes a standards family rather than a guarantee of one fixed speed everywhere. Coverage, congestion and network design still determine real performance.

sections.title: Satellites, orbits and navigation distinctions
sections.text:
**Geostationary orbit.**

A geostationary satellite orbits approximately **35,786 km** above Earth's equator. Its orbital period equals Earth's sidereal rotation period of about 23 hours, 56 minutes and 4 seconds—not exactly the ordinary 24-hour solar day. The orbit is equatorial and essentially circular.

**Uplink and downlink.**

**Uplink:** Signal traveling from a ground station to the satellite.

**Downlink:** Signal traveling from the satellite toward Earth.

**Crosslink:** Communication between satellites.

**Why does GEO communication have noticeable latency.**

Consider an idealized direct satellite relay in which a signal travels: Ground A → GEO satellite → Ground B. Even ignoring equipment processing, the propagation distance is at least roughly twice GEO altitude in a favorable geometry.

$$2\times35{,}786=71{,}572\text{ km}$$

At approximately 300,000 km/s:

$$t\approx\frac{71{,}572}{300{,}000}\approx0.239\text{ seconds}$$

That is only the approximate one-way propagation for this simplified two-leg relay geometry. A request and return response may involve at least four such ground–space legs, plus other network and processing delays. This explains why GEO latency cannot simply be eliminated by increasing bandwidth.

A communications transponder receives an uplink, amplifies and commonly frequency-translates it, and transmits a downlink. Some satellites process or route information onboard. Higher-frequency microwave links can experience rain attenuation through absorption and scattering. Antenna gain, transmitter power, receiver sensitivity and atmospheric loss contribute to a link budget.

A geostationary relay requires at least roughly two ground–space legs for one-way communication between two ground terminals. Using an ideal minimum path of $2\times35,786$ km and propagation speed of about 300,000 km/s gives 0.239 seconds. A request and response involve at least four legs, producing about 0.477 seconds of ideal propagation before additional network and processing delays. Orbit geometry usually increases the path beyond this favourable estimate.

**PakSAT-MM1.**

Pakistan's Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO) identifies **PakSAT-MM1** as a communications satellite designed for broadband, television broadcasting, cellular backhaul and VSAT services. Its published orbital longitude is **38.2°E** and the satellite carries C-, Ku-, Ka- and L-band capabilities for specified applications. The quoted longitude is an orbital slot, not an altitude.

**PRSC-EO2 — Earth observation.**

SUPARCO reports that **PRSC-EO2**, an electro-optical remote-sensing satellite, was launched on **12 February 2026** into an approximately 520 km sun-synchronous orbit. Its described applications include agriculture, urban planning, water-resource monitoring and disaster management. This is a useful comparison:

**PakSAT-MM1:** Communication service.

**PRSC-EO2:** Observation of Earth's surface.

Neither should be confused with the GPS navigation constellation.

PakSAT-MM1 is a communication mission; PRSC-EO2 is an Earth-observation mission; a GNSS constellation broadcasts positioning and timing signals. These functions differ even when all three technologies use orbiting spacecraft. SUPARCO identifies PakSAT-MM1's service roles and PRSC-EO2's 12 February 2026 launch. [SUPARCO: PakSAT-MM1](https://suparco.gov.pk/major-programmes-satellite-programs/paksat-mm1.html), [SUPARCO: PRSC-EO2](https://suparco.gov.pk/major-programmes-satellite-programs/eo-2.html).

sections.title: Optical fibre and radar ranging
sections.text:
**optical fiber.**

Optical fiber is a thin, transparent waveguide, commonly made of glass, that carries light signals over distance. Information is encoded into optical signals, transmitted through the fiber and detected at the receiving end. Modern optical networks support high-capacity communication within and between countries.

**Three basic fiber components.**

**Core:** Central region carrying guided optical modes.

**Cladding:** Surrounding material with lower refractive index, helping confine the light.

**Protective coating:** Helps protect the fiber from mechanical damage and environmental exposure.

**total internal reflection.**

Total internal reflection can occur when light traveling through a higher-refractive-index medium encounters a lower-index medium at an incidence angle greater than the critical angle. For an appropriate interface:

$$\boxed{\sin\theta_c=\frac{n_2}{n_1}}$$

where $n_1>n_2$, and the incidence angle is measured from the normal to the interface. Properly designed fiber optics exploit optical confinement associated with the core–cladding refractive-index structure.

**Single-mode versus multimode fiber.**

| Single-mode | Multimode |
|---|---|
| Supports one spatial mode under specified operating conditions | Supports multiple spatial modes |
| Common in long-haul networks | Common in certain shorter-range networks |
| Lower modal-dispersion limitations | Greater modal-dispersion constraints |
| Often used with laser sources | Can use appropriate lasers or other optical sources |

Optical attenuation reduces signal power, while dispersion spreads pulses and can limit distinguishable symbol rates. Single-mode fibre avoids intermodal dispersion but still has other dispersion and attenuation mechanisms. Wavelength-division multiplexing carries separate channels using different optical wavelengths. Fibre has high capacity and resists electromagnetic interference, but installation and physical protection remain necessary.

Radar range in a simple monostatic arrangement is $R=ct/2$, where $R$ is metres, $c$ is signal propagation speed in metres per second and $t$ is round-trip time in seconds. A 20-microsecond delay gives approximately $3\times10^8\times20\times10^{-6}/2=3000$ metres. The factor of two accounts for outward and return travel. Doppler measurements can provide radial-motion information, while imaging radar is developed in Chapter 19.

questions.prompt: Which statement distinguishes the Internet from the World Wide Web?

options.A: The internet is an interconnected network system; the web is one service operating over it
options.B: Both describe exactly one commercial website
options.C: The web existed before computer networks in their modern form

questions.explanation: The web uses protocols such as HTTP over internet infrastructure, but many non-web services also exist.

questions.prompt: Which device normally forwards IP packets between different networks?
questions.explanation: Routers use network-layer information and routing decisions to forward packets.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is responsible for distributed domain-name resolution?
questions.explanation: DNS provides a distributed system for looking up domain-related records such as IP addresses.

questions.prompt: IPv6 addresses have a length of:
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, compared with IPv4's 32-bit addresses.

questions.prompt: Which difference between TCP and UDP is accurate?

options.A: TCP provides a reliable ordered byte stream; UDP by itself does not guarantee delivery

questions.explanation: TCP supplies reliability and ordering; UDP supplies connectionless datagrams.

questions.prompt: HTTP/3 commonly uses which transport technology?
questions.explanation: HTTP/3 uses QUIC, which runs over UDP and integrates modern security and transport features.

questions.prompt: Which statement about HTTPS is correct?

options.A: It guarantees every website is honest
options.B: It protects communication using secure transport but does not establish the truthfulness of content
options.C: It is the same as a physical firewall
options.D: It requires web pages to contain no images

questions.explanation: HTTPS provides transport security but does not prove that a site is legitimate or its content factual.

questions.prompt: Which is a typical example of application-layer communication?
questions.explanation: HTTP is an application-layer protocol for transferring web resources.

questions.prompt: A radio system changes the phase of its carrier among a set of permitted values to represent digital symbols. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Phase-shift keying encodes digital symbols using selected carrier phase states.

questions.prompt: A receiver obtains a strong carrier but cannot recover information because substantial interfering noise occupies the relevant channel. Which measure best describes the relative strength of the wanted signal and noise?
questions.explanation: SNR compares desired signal power with noise power and is important for communication reliability.

questions.prompt: Which operation allows different optical wavelengths to carry separate information streams through the same fiber?
questions.explanation: WDM sends information channels using different optical wavelengths through one suitable fiber.

questions.prompt: A digital receiver identifies an erroneous transmission using a parity check. Which conclusion is most defensible?

options.A: The receiver has necessarily corrected every possible error
options.B: No bit can ever be corrupted
options.C: The channel has become completely noise-free
options.D: Parity can detect certain error patterns without guaranteeing correction

questions.explanation: Parity is an error-detection technique with limitations; a simple parity bit does not correct arbitrary errors.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of dividing a mobile-service region into multiple radio cells?

options.B: Allowing geographically managed coverage and reuse of spectrum resources
options.C: Replacing all network servers with batteries
options.D: Ensuring every mobile device uses a unique global frequency

questions.explanation: Cellular organization improves coverage and capacity through distributed base stations and controlled reuse.

questions.prompt: A moving phone retains its ongoing call while the serving radio connection transfers to a nearby base station. This is:
questions.explanation: Handover transfers a serving connection as coverage or network conditions change.

questions.prompt: Why can a fixed Earth antenna remain aimed at the same geostationary satellite?

options.A: The satellite's circular equatorial orbit matches Earth's rotational period and direction
options.B: Gravity is absent at GEO altitude
options.C: The satellite moves in a polar orbit every 90 minutes
options.D: The satellite is physically attached to Earth

questions.explanation: A suitable geostationary orbit makes the satellite appear fixed over one longitude.

questions.prompt: A GEO broadband link has adequate bandwidth but a noticeable minimum propagation delay. What is the principal physical reason?

options.A: The satellite cannot transmit digital data
options.C: Microwaves move slower than sound in vacuum
options.D: The signal must travel a long ground–space path at a finite propagation speed

questions.explanation: Large signal travel distance produces latency even when the available data capacity is high.

questions.prompt: A conventional bent-pipe satellite receives a microwave uplink and retransmits it using a different radio frequency. Which component performs this general relay function?
questions.explanation: A conventional transponder receives, amplifies and often frequency-translates the radio signal.

questions.prompt: Why may a high-frequency satellite link suffer reduced quality during intense rainfall?

options.A: Rain permanently removes the satellite from orbit
options.B: Rain stops all electrical current on Earth
options.C: Rain-related absorption and scattering can attenuate the radio signal
options.D: Clouds destroy all digital encryption keys

questions.explanation: Rain fade affects suitable microwave bands, especially certain higher-frequency satellite links.

questions.prompt: For guided light confinement in an ordinary step-index fiber, which refractive-index relationship is generally required?

options.A: Core refractive index exceeds cladding refractive index
options.B: Cladding index must always be greater than core index
options.C: Both refractive indices must be exactly zero
options.D: Light must propagate without any electromagnetic field

questions.explanation: A higher-index core surrounded by lower-index cladding supports guided optical modes.

questions.prompt: Why is single-mode optical fiber especially useful for long-distance high-capacity links?

options.C: It eliminates all need for optical receivers
options.D: It avoids the intermodal dispersion associated with multiple spatial propagation modes

questions.explanation: Single-mode operation avoids intermodal dispersion; chromatic dispersion and attenuation still require engineering.

questions.prompt: A radar pulse takes a measured time to travel to a target and return. Why is the measured total distance divided by two when calculating target range?

options.A: Radio waves only carry half the required energy
options.C: The pulse travels to the target and back
options.D: The atmosphere contains two oxygen atoms

questions.explanation: A monostatic radar measures a round-trip delay, so one-way target range uses half the propagation distance.

questions.prompt: A DNS resolver stores a recent domain lookup temporarily. Which effect is expected?

options.A: All domain names become permanent IP addresses
options.C: Repeated lookup time can decrease, although cached records may become outdated
options.D: The computer no longer uses network protocols

questions.explanation: DNS caching reduces repeated resolution work but must respect expiration and changes in authoritative records.

questions.prompt: A home router lets many private-addressed devices access the internet through limited public address resources. Which mechanism commonly helps?
questions.explanation: NAT can translate private addresses and ports to support connections through a smaller pool of public addresses.

questions.prompt: A browser displays a valid HTTPS certificate for a particular domain. What has this NOT automatically established?

options.A: That TLS can support authenticated encrypted transport
options.B: That the certificate is associated with the domain under the trust system
options.C: That communication integrity can be protected
options.D: That every statement or financial offer on the website is truthful

questions.explanation: HTTPS authenticates the server/domain under certificate assumptions; it does not verify the operator's honesty or content accuracy.

questions.prompt: When a TCP sender detects signs of network congestion, what is a typical protocol response?

options.A: Increase transmission infinitely regardless of congestion
options.B: Reduce or adapt the sending rate according to congestion-control behavior

questions.explanation: TCP congestion control adjusts transmission behavior to help avoid worsening network congestion.

analytical.prompt: Explain computer networking and the TCP/IP architecture. Describe what happens when a user opens a secure website.
analytical.answer_html:
Introduction

Computer networking enables devices to exchange information through physical communication links and standardized protocols. The internet interconnects many networks using the TCP/IP protocol family.

Network devices

Network interfaces transmit and receive data. Switches connect devices within local networks. Routers forward IP packets between networks.

IP addressing

Internet Protocol provides addressing and routing functions. IPv4 and IPv6 use different address sizes and formats.

Transport protocols

TCP provides reliable ordered byte-stream communication. UDP supplies datagram transport without built-in guaranteed delivery. Modern QUIC can provide secure reliable communication over UDP.

DNS

The Domain Name System provides distributed lookup of domain-related records, including IP addresses.

HTTPS

HTTP defines web requests and responses. HTTPS protects these communications through suitable secure transport technologies, commonly TLS or QUIC-integrated TLS.

Loading a webpage

The browser identifies the requested website and resolves necessary addresses. A secure connection is established. The browser sends an HTTP request. The server processes it and returns data. The browser interprets the response and renders the webpage.

Conclusion

Internet communication depends on cooperation among naming systems, network addressing, transport protocols, server software and the browser.

analytical.prompt: Explain the complete mechanism of wireless communication and critically differentiate analog, digital and fiber-optic transmission.
analytical.answer_html:
Introduction

Telecommunication is the exchange of information over a distance through physical signals. It can use guided media such as fiber optics or unguided electromagnetic propagation such as radio waves.

Transmitter and receiver

A transmitter converts information into a suitable signal. It may perform source coding, error-control coding, modulation and signal amplification. The signal travels through a communication channel. A receiver detects the signal, performs appropriate demodulation and decoding, and recovers the intended information.

Analog communication

Analog methods represent information through continuous changes in signal characteristics. AM varies amplitude, while FM varies instantaneous frequency. Noise can distort the received information.

Digital communication

Digital communication represents information through discrete symbols. Appropriate coding can support error detection and correction. Digital systems also permit efficient compression, encryption and signal processing.

Fiber-optic communication

Optical fiber guides light through a refractive-index structure consisting of a core and cladding. Data are transmitted by modulating optical signals. Fiber offers high capacity, low attenuation and resistance to electromagnetic interference.

Comparison

Wireless systems provide mobility and coverage without continuous physical cabling to the user. Fiber systems require physical installation but are particularly valuable for high-capacity backbone links.

Conclusion

Modern communication networks use a combination of wireless links and optical fibers. Their reliability depends on proper modulation, bandwidth allocation, signal quality and network architecture.

analytical.prompt: Explain how satellite communication operates. Compare geostationary and low Earth orbit systems with reference to Pakistan.
analytical.answer_html:
Introduction

Satellite communication uses spacecraft to receive, process or relay electromagnetic signals between suitable communication terminals.

Uplink

A ground transmitter encodes and modulates information onto a radio-frequency carrier. An antenna directs the signal toward the spacecraft.

Satellite payload

A conventional transponder receives the signal, amplifies it, often changes its frequency and retransmits it. More advanced satellites may perform digital signal processing or switching onboard.

Downlink

A receiving ground terminal collects the signal and recovers the represented information.

Geostationary satellites

A GEO satellite orbits above Earth's equator at approximately 35,786 km altitude. Its orbital period matches Earth's rotation, making it appear nearly stationary. This supports fixed communication antennas and wide-area broadcasting. However, the long propagation path introduces substantial latency.

Low Earth orbit satellites

LEO satellites move relatively rapidly across the sky. They can provide shorter propagation paths but often require constellations, tracking or handover to maintain continuous coverage.

Pakistan example

SUPARCO identifies PakSAT-MM1 as a communications satellite supporting broadband and broadcasting services. Its PRSC-EO2 satellite has a different mission: collecting Earth-observation imagery.

Conclusion

Communication satellites and remote-sensing satellites serve different primary purposes. Orbit selection involves trade-offs among coverage, latency, constellation size and mission requirements.

analytical.prompt: Describe mobile communication architecture and explain the roles of cellular networks, frequency reuse, handover and 5G.
analytical.answer_html:
Introduction

Mobile communication uses radio-frequency links to connect moving users with a communication network. The cellular model divides large service regions into manageable coverage areas.

Cellular architecture

A mobile device communicates with a serving base station. The base station connects through transport and core-network infrastructure to other services.

Frequency reuse

Careful reuse of spectrum across different cells improves network capacity. Interference must be managed using frequency planning, scheduling and other techniques.

Handover

As a device moves between coverage regions, the network can transfer its serving connection from one cell to another. Successful handover supports continuity of communication.

Mobile generations

Earlier mobile systems concentrated on voice. Subsequent generations expanded digital data capabilities. 4G supports mobile broadband, while 5G standards address enhanced broadband, low-latency applications and machine-type communication.

Challenges

Radio obstruction, congestion, spectrum limitations, interference and network resilience affect performance.

Conclusion

Mobile communication is a combination of radio physics, networking and real-time resource management rather than a single transmitting tower.
